explanation: Try every possible starting character index. Split the candidate into word-sized chunks and count their frequencies, rejecting an unknown word or a count above the required multiplicity. Exactly m accepted chunks consume the entire requested multiset.
timeComplexity: O(mw + n·m·w) expected worst-case time for text length n, m words of width w: each of O(n) starts checks at most m copied/hashed chunks.
spaceComplexity: O(mw) auxiliary character storage for required and current chunk counts, plus O(r) output for r matches.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/string_decompositions_into_dictionary_words.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Every valid concatenation has a starting index in the examined range and consists of m chunks of the common word length. A rejected chunk is absent from the required multiset or exceeds its allowed count, so that candidate cannot match. If all m chunks respect the required counts, their total count equals the multiset size, forcing every multiplicity to match exactly.
walkthrough: For xoakashashoakz and [oak,ash], each word has width 3. Candidate 1 splits into oak|ash and matches. Candidate 4 splits into ash|ash and exceeds ash’s count. Candidate 7 splits into ash|oak and matches. Other starts contain an unknown chunk; return [1,7].
edgeCases: Repeated supplied words require their full multiplicities.
Matches can overlap and can begin in different word alignments.
All supplied words share one positive length; text shorter than their combined length has no match.
